title: Audit evidence handshake and event taxonomy notes v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This note collects a pragmatic proposal for an "audit evidence handshake" pattern plus a compact event taxonomy we can iterate on for v1->v3 of the audit schema. The goal is to reduce downstream SIEM cost and simplify evidence automation while preserving forensic fidelity and RBAC v2 semantics.

Context & motivation:
- We have many producers (console, private deployments, dedicated runtime) emitting events with different shapes.
- SIEM exports and evidence automation currently duplicate payloads and introduce heavy indexing costs.
- Teams need a way to know what evidence is available without transferring raw payloads except when needed for investigations.
- RBAC v2 introduces richer principal and role metadata that should be surfaced in the audit envelope (not leaked into evidence unless authorized).

Design principles:
- Minimal event envelope at source: small, strongly-typed fields for routing and provenance.
- Evidence handshake: producers publish compact evidence descriptors (metdata + secure pointer + checksum) and a separate evidence store exchange protocol pulls raw data on demand.
- Compatibility-first versioning: semantic-style major.minor.patch where major increments are breaking; minor adds optional fields; patch for fixes. Producer/consumer capability headers exchanged in the handshake.
- Redaction by intent: events explicitly label which fields are PII/evidence and whether pointers should be included in SIEM exports.

Proposed compact event envelope (example snippet - illustrative):

{
  "event_id": "evt_20260309_12a3f",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-09T12:34:56Z",
  "type": "auth.login.attempt",
  "outcome": "failure",
  "actor_id": "user:U12345",
  "actor_role_summary": "admin:billing",
  "resource": "project:proj-9",
  "service": "console",
  "evidence_refs": [
    {
      "evidence_id": "evid_9b7f",
      "kind": "http-body",
      "store": "evidence-store://us-west/objs/9b7f",
      "digest_sha256": "fa3b...",
      "size_bytes": 4500,
      "access_policy": "on_demand_with_audit"
    }
  ],
  "schema_version": "audit.v1.2",
  "producer_capabilities": ["evidence-handshake:v1", "rbac-enrichment:v2"]
}

Notes on fields:
- evidence_refs is intentionally lightweight: pointer, type, checksum, size, and a short access policy.
- actor_role_summary is a stable short string used for rapid filtering; full role and claims live in role_store and are fetched by evidence/forensic flows if necessary.
- schema_version uses a namespace (audit.v) to avoid collision with other product schemas.

Evidence handshake flow (high level):
1) Producer emits event with evidence_refs and capability header.
2) Indexer/SIEM stores the compact envelope. By default, raw evidence payloads are NOT forwarded to external SIEMs unless the export policy is explicit.
3) When SOC or SRE needs raw evidence, they request it via evidence-store service using evidence_id + justification. The store enforces RBAC checks (based on requestor identity and access_policy) and writes audit proof of access.
4) Evidence pull is logged as a separate audit event with cross-reference to original event_id and evidence_id.

Versioning and backcompat strategy:
- Major (vX.*): breaking change (rename core fields, remove evidence_refs). Require producers and consumers to register a migration plan in the schema registry.
- Minor (v0.Y): additive: new optional fields, new evidence kinds. Consumers must ignore unknown fields.
- Patch: non-structural fixes only.
- Compatibility header: every event may include "producer_capabilities": [..] and consumers can respond with an "ack_schema" signal. During upgrade windows, indexers should accept multiple schema versions concurrently and tag events with detected version.

SIEM export considerations (reduce cost):
- Default SIEM export should omit evidence payloads and only include evidence_refs.
- Provide a configurable mapping profile for different SIEMs (CEF/LEEF/Elastic) that controls whether actor_role_summary is expanded or redacted.
- Example CEF mapping (pseudo):
  - cef.deviceVendor=Redwood
  - cef.deviceProduct=inference
  - cef.eventId = event_id
  - extension.actor = actor_id
  - extension.actorRole = actor_role_summary
  - extension.evidenceRef = evidence_refs[0].evidence_id

RBAC v2 integration notes:
- We must avoid embedding full role claim sets in exported SIEM events. Use role summaries and role reference ids (role_ref).
- The evidence-store must consult RBAC v2 authorization (policy decision point) on every pull. Pulls must be logged with the decision result (allow/deny) and policy_version.
- For private deployments, the handshake should carry a deployment-scoped tenant id and trust root fingerprint.

Evidence automation and retention:
- Evidence descriptors include retention_class (ephemeral/standard/longterm) and deletion_date. Evidence-store enforces lifecycle and emits lifecycle events on delete or archive.
- To support automated incident playbooks, we add evidence_tags that can be used for auto-collection rules (e.g., "PII-suspect", "privileged-actor").

Security considerations:
- Pointers must be signed (HMAC or RSA) with producer key to prevent pointer forging in transit. Evidence-store should verify pointer signature and digest before serving.
- Pointer TTLs should be short; refresh flow exists for long-running investigations. Each pointer refresh is logged.
- Indexer-to-evidence-store communication must be authenticated and minimized (pull by request only unless export policy allows push).

Migration checklist (for rollout from v1 -> v2):
- [ ] Publish schema v2 draft and field contracts in registry.
- [ ] Add producer capability headers to all producers.
- [ ] Deploy evidence-store maturity endpoint (check digest, access policy enforcement).
- [ ] Run dual-write indexer accepting v1/v2 for 30 days.
- [ ] Enable canary SIEM export profile that exercises redaction rules.
- [ ] Update runbooks and SOC playbooks to use evidence pull APIs.

Open questions / decisions required:
- How do we handle large streaming evidence (e.g., full request/response logs > 50MB)? Prefer chunked evidence objects with a single evidence_id and chunk index, or treat large items as archive-only?
- Can we adopt a standard pointer URI format (evidence-store://...) across private deployments? Requires agreement on auth mechanisms.
- Should evidence_refs be encrypted at rest in the indexer to reduce accidental leaks (tradeoff: more complexity for indexing/search)?

Action items (next steps):
- Priya to draft a concise schema registry entry for audit.v1.2 reflecting this handshake (due 2026-03-17).
- Liam to prototype pointer signing and verification in evidence-store (POC by 2026-04-01).
- Maya to produce a SIEM export mapping template for Splunk and Elastic that omits raw evidence by default (review 2026-03-24).
- Security WG to decide on chunking vs archive model by 2026-03-31.

Appendix: example event -> evidence pull trace (human readable):
- event evt_20260309_12a3f emitted with evidence_refs [evid_9b7f]
- analyst requests evidence via evidence-store API with justification "incident-2026-003"
- PDP returns allow with policy_version=rbacv2-2026-02
- evidence-store returns signed URL (short TTL). Access is logged as audit.pull.evidence with link back to evt_20260309_12a3f

References and related work:
- Existing audit-schema playbooks (see linked artifacts)
- RBAC v2 design doc (security-and-compliance/arch/rbac-v2-overview)
- SIEM export guidelines (GTM/SIEM-mapping)

This is a working note — expect edits and refinement. Please add comments in-line or suggest changes through JIRA SEC-9812.
